data.content_ref: inline:The current consensus on undecidability (SRC_001, SRC_002, SRC_003, SRC_004, SRC_005) contradicts the school stance of 'anchor in cases' by shifting the problem from empirical search to meta-logical impossibility. Specifically, the claim that the conjecture is unsettled because it is a Universal Turing Machine (UTM) implies that no search for counterexamples (cycles or divergence) will ever yield a general result. This relation is refuted if a concrete counterexample is discovered or if a proof is constructed in ZFC.
